newsitem.title: UK: Britain's NAAFI chooses Spar as retail partner.
newsitem.headline: Britain's NAAFI chooses Spar as retail partner.

text.p: Britain's NAAFI, originally set up to feed the country's armed forces, said on Wednesday it will team up with retailer Spar to modernise its 200 stores.
The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) said Spar will be its partner in a wide ranging restructuring programme worth 500 million pounds over the next five years.
Spar will provide staff training and development, distribution and logistics and information technology as well as Spar branded goods.
Spar was chosen after extensive trials, which also included retailers Londis and Costcutter.
Spar, a private company based in the Netherlands, operates stores on a franchise basis and has outlets in 27 countries. It has 2,500 outlets in Britain.

The NAAFI will spend 10 million pounds ($15.9 million) modernising its stores, which are spread across the country. They will continue to be run and staffed by NAAFI personnel. Four NAAFI shops were converted to a Spar format as a trial and these increased sales by more than 50 percent.
NAAFI chief executive Geoffrey Dart said the restructuring was designed to return the stores to profitability.
The modernisation programme will start in May and all stores are due to receive their facelift by April 1998.
Earlier this year the NAAFI lost its traditional role of supplying canteens around the world for the British armed forces to food and distribution group Booker Group Plc.
It was formed in 1921 to provide canteen services to the navy, army and air force. It is now focusing on retail and leisure activities. -- London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717 ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
